### Description

Trying to use a datasource to look up an azuread_application by name and receiving this error:

```
 Error: Multiple applications found
│ 
│   with module.foo.data.azuread_application.this,
│   on .terraform/modules/.../datasources.tf line 1, in data "azuread_application" "this":
│    1: data "azuread_application" "this" {
│ 
│ Found multiple applications matching filter: "displayName eq
│ 'myapp'"
```

Problem is that we have more than one application with the same name. I think some of our apps have been deleted, only one appears in searching in portal.azure, but they remain in the catalog, and the deletedDateTime is null for all of them. The Graph API returns all 2 or 3 apps, so I'm not sure how to distinguish the "real" one, except for the creation date being the latest. 

Therefore I would like to be able to return a single app with the most recent created date, in the event that there are more than one app found by name.

### Description

Currently Oauth2 permissions can be read for an application, but not set. It would be nice to add support for setting Oauth2 permissions as well (exposing APIs). However normally it's hard to maintain all Oauth2 permissions in Terraform, since some would be automatically created outside of Terraform. And such the suggestion is to add separate resource `azuread_application_oauth2_permission` for this.

I am happy to create a PR for this.

<!--- Please leave a helpful description of the feature request here. --->

### New or Affected Resource(s)

<!--- Please list the new or affected resources and data sources. --->

* azuread_application_oauth2_permission

### Potential Terraform Configuration

<!--- Information about code formatting: https://help.github.com/articles/basic-writing-and-formatting-syntax/#quoting-code --->

```hcl
resource "azuread_application_oauth2_permission" "test" {
  application_object_id = azuread_application.main.object_id

  type = "User"

  admin_consent_description = "Allow access to example on behalf of the signed-in user."
  admin_consent_display_name = "Access example"

  user_consent_description = "Allow access to example on your behalf."
  user_consent_display_name = "Access example"

  value = "user_impersonation"
}
```

Terraform azuread_application oauth2_permissions issue on second apply only

_This issue was originally opened by @scott-doyland-burrows as hashicorp/terraform#26672. It was migrated here as a result of the [provider split](https://www.hashicorp.com/blog/upcoming-provider-changes-in-terraform-0-10/). The original body of the issue is below._
    
<hr>

```
+ provider registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/azuread v1.0.0
```

### Terraform Configuration Files

```
  name = "example"
  oauth2_permissions = []
```

Terraform should ignore the type field.

```
        homepage                   = "https://client-app"
        name                       = "client-app"
        oauth2_allow_implicit_flow = true

        reply_urls                 = [

    }
```

### Affected Resource(s)

### Terraform Configuration Files
The **oauth2_permission_scope** block is specified without **type**
```hcl
resource "azuread_application" "app-test01" {
  display_name = "app-test01"
  api {
    oauth2_permission_scope {
      id                         = "c8c8c26a-d30e-4135-886f-490ea092e7b8"
      admin_consent_display_name = "Read-only access to Employee records"
      admin_consent_description  = "Allow the application to have read-only access to all Employee data."
      value                      = "Employees.Read.All"
    }
  }
}
```
### Expected Behavior
* The **type** parameter should be marked as **Optional** in the documentation.

### Actual Behavior
* The **type** parameter has been marked as **Required** in the documentation.

* The 'Required' specification **conflicts** with the displayed behavior and the parameter description that **type** defaults to **User**.

**Terraform apply (oauth2_permission_scope block specified without type)**
```hcl
Terraform will perform the following actions:

  # azuread_application.app-test01 will be created
  + resource "azuread_application" "app-test01" {
     ...
      + api {
          + requested_access_token_version = 1
          + oauth2_permission_scope {
              + admin_consent_description  = "Allow the application to have read-only access to all Employee data."
              + admin_consent_display_name = "Read-only access to Employee records"
              + enabled                    = true
              + id                         = "c8c8c26a-d30e-4135-886f-490ea092e7b8"
              + type                       = "User"  # Defaults to User. Parameter isn't specified in the terraform configuration
              + value                      = "Employees.Read.All"
            }
        }
    }

Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy.
```

1. `terraform apply` (without type in oauth2-permission_scope block)

* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment

### Terraform (and AzureAD Provider) Version

```
Terraform v1.13.3
+ provider registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/azuread v3.0.2
```

### Affected Resource(s)

* `azuread_group`

### Terraform Configuration Files

```hcl
resource "azuread_group" "example" {
  display_name     = "My_Group"
  mail_nickname    = "My_Group"
  mail_enabled     = false
  security_enabled = true
}
```

When the group already exists with an auto-generated `mail_nickname` (e.g., `cf11bd75-2`) and you add or change `mail_nickname` to a meaningful value, Terraform plans a forced replacement.

### Debug Output

```
~ mail_nickname = "cf11bd75-2" -> "My_Group" # forces replacement
```

### Expected Behavior

Changing `mail_nickname` should update the group in-place. The Microsoft Graph API supports updating `mailNickname` via PATCH without recreating the group:

```bash
az rest --method PATCH \
  --url "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups/<group-id>" \
  --body '{"mailNickname": "My_Group"}'
```

This works and updates the attribute without destroying the group or its memberships/assignments.

### Actual Behavior

Terraform plans a destroy + create (forced replacement) when `mail_nickname` is changed. This is destructive for groups that have:
- Members
- App role assignments (e.g., SCIM provisioning, SSO)
- Downstream dependencies (e.g., Cloud Identity group sync)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an `azuread_group` without specifying `mail_nickname` (Azure auto-generates one)
2. Import or apply the group
3. Add `mail_nickname = "meaningful_value"` to the resource
4. Run `terraform plan` - observe `# forces replacement`

### Important Factoids

The workaround is to update `mailNickname` directly via the Graph API and then Terraform shows no changes.

### References

* Microsoft Graph API docs confirm PATCH support for `mailNickname`: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/group-update

### Expected Behavior

Running _terraform plan_ or _terraform apply_ should still find the azuread_group it created (or was imported) earlier , regardless of the object's `membershipRule` setting. This was the behaviour of provider <= 1.6.

### Actual Behavior

Terraform does not detect the group any longer and aims at creating a fresh one. Depending on the setting of `prevent_duplicate_names` it will either create an additional copy or refuse the creation (see output above).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `terraform apply`
2. manually change the created AzureAD group to have a dynamic membership rule (any will do)
3. `terraform plan`

### Important Factoids

I am porting terraform workflows to provider 2.x. In some cases groups created initially via terraform, are turned into dynamic membership groups by a Graph API call _after_ terraform apply.
Nonetheless those groups are kept in terraform state in order to support referencing them (e.g. for azurerm RBAC rules) as well as to support future `display_name`, `description` and `owner` changes.
This process works perfectly on azuread provider <= 1.6
I do realize that actual support for `membershipRule` might be on the roadmap already but as long as this is not implemented, the provider should also consider and check if groups are already in its state _regardless of their membershipRule_ attribute.

azuread_application performs invalid full PATCH for owners-only updates on legacy SAML identifierUris

### Terraform and provider version

- Terraform: 1.12.x
- Provider: hashicorp/azuread v3.9.0
- Microsoft Graph API: v1.0

### Affected resource

- `azuread_application`

### Context

An existing single-tenant SAML application has a legacy SAML entity ID stored in `identifierUris` with a trailing slash, for example:

```text
https://sso.example.invalid/accounts/saml/client/metadata/
```

The trailing slash is required by the external SAML relying party. The application was originally created/configured outside Terraform. Microsoft Graph permits the existing value to be read and retained, but rejects application PATCH requests containing it with:

```text
IdentifierUrisEndsWithSlash: Application alias value is invalid.
```

This is related to #1728 and the validation change in #928.

### Reproduction

Import an existing application with a trailing-slash SAML `identifierUris` value, then configure an unrelated owner change:

```hcl
resource "azuread_application" "example" {
  display_name    = "Existing SAML application"
  identifier_uris = ["https://sso.example.invalid/accounts/saml/client/metadata/"]
  owners         = ["00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"]

  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [identifier_uris]
  }
}
```

After import, when only `owners` differs, Terraform plans an owners-only update. Apply still fails with `IdentifierUrisEndsWithSlash`.

### Actual behavior

The provider executes `UpdateApplication` before its separate owner reconciliation. The exact v3.9.0 source is:

- `applicationResourceUpdate` starts at [line 1314](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azuread/blob/v3.9.0/internal/services/applications/application_resource.go#L1314).
- The application PATCH is invoked at [line 1542](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azuread/blob/v3.9.0/internal/services/applications/application_resource.go#L1542).
- Owner reconciliation starts at [line 1556](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azuread/blob/v3.9.0/internal/services/applications/application_resource.go#L1556).
- The dedicated owner resource calls `AddOwnerRef` at [line 111](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azuread/blob/v3.9.0/internal/services/applications/application_owner_resource.go#L111).

`ignore_changes = [identifier_uris]` suppresses the Terraform diff but does not prevent the provider/Graph client from validating the existing URI during the unrelated application PATCH.

### Expected behavior

When only application owners change, `azuread_application` should not issue a general application PATCH containing unrelated application properties. It should either:

1. Skip `UpdateApplication` when no mutable application properties changed and reconcile owners using the dedicated owner endpoint, or
2. Use the dedicated owner resource behavior for owner-only changes.

This would preserve existing SAML entity IDs while allowing ownership reconciliation.

### Workaround

Avoid changing `owners` through `azuread_application` and manage ownership separately using `azuread_application_owner`, or manage the application ownership manually. This is not currently possible without also changing the resource model because `azuread_application_owner` is documented as incompatible with `azuread_application` for the same application.

### References

- Existing trailing-slash behavior: https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azuread/issues/1728
- Identifier URI validation change: https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azuread/pull/928
- Microsoft Graph application `identifierUris`: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/application?view=graph-rest-1.0#identifieruris-attribute


### Expected Behavior

The last member from the AD group should be deleted, result should be empty AzureAD group with no members.

### Actual Behavior

1. If a azuread_group has multiple members, you can successfully remove all but one member. There will always be one member which remains even though the terraform configuration has none.
2. If the azuread_group has a single member, you can remove it from the terraform configuration and also apply without failure however no DELETE action is triggered for the final member. This means in AzureAD Group that member still exists. In all subsequent terraform plans you will see one member being removed as there are none defined in the terraform configuration, apply will be successful however the member will not be deleted from the AzureAD group.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an `azuread_group` resource with multiple members defined.
2. `terraform apply`
3. Remove all members from the the `azuread_group` resource.
3. `terraform apply`

<!--- Thank you for keeping this note for the community --->

### Description

I was recently investigating creation of VDPOOLs and ADDS users, along with the domain to spring up complete infrastructure which would allow for remote application access via an AVD. As part of this research process, I observed that terraform does not have a method of performing password reset on azuread_user provider. Terraform needs that ability to reset ADDS passwords for users in order to comply with Microsoft design as outlined below.
 
"""
To authenticate users on the managed domain, Azure AD DS needs password hashes in a format that's suitable for NT LAN Manager (NTLM) and Kerberos authentication. Azure AD doesn't generate or store password hashes in the format that's required for NTLM or Kerberos authentication until you enable Azure AD DS for your tenant. For security reasons, Azure AD also doesn't store any password credentials in clear-text form. Therefore, Azure AD can't automatically generate these NTLM or Kerberos password hashes based on users' existing credentials. The steps to generate and store these password hashes are different for cloud-only user accounts created in Azure AD versus user accounts that are synchronized from your on-premises directory using Azure AD Connect.

A cloud-only user account is an account that was created in your Azure AD directory using either the Azure portal or Azure AD PowerShell cmdlets. These user accounts aren't synchronized from an on-premises directory. For cloud-only user accounts, users must change their passwords before they can use Azure AD DS. This password change process causes the password hashes for Kerberos and NTLM authentication to be generated and stored in Azure AD. The account isn't synchronized from Azure AD to Azure AD DS until the password is changed. Either expire the passwords for all cloud users in the tenant who need to use Azure AD DS, which forces a password change on next sign-in, or instruct cloud users to manually change their passwords. 

"""

Because of the password management design, it effectively removes the ability create new ADDS accounts to perform administrative actions such as joining the AVD systems to the AD domain as, without password reset, the account won't have NTLM hashes needed for the process to succeed. This results in JsonADDomainExtension failing on AVD creation.

### New or Affected Resource(s)

* azuread_user 

### Potential Terraform Configuration

```hcl
resource "azuread_user" "dc_admin" {
  user_principal_name              = "test@test.onmicrosoft.com"
  display_name                         = "AADDS DC Administrator"
  password                               = "Helo1235%"
  force_password_change       = false
  account_enabled                   = true
  disable_password_expiration = true
  reset_password                      = true # This would reset password to random value and set it back to original password 
}
```

* https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory-domain-services/tutorial-create-instance#enable-user-accounts-for-azure-ad-ds

### Description

<!--- Please leave a helpful description of the feature request here. --->

If you create new AD group, you cannot add your user object_id to a list of the group owners.
In new version of terraform you do not need to add yourself as owner during the group update, and the results are:
* no exception is thrown
* you can delete yourself from existing ADGroup.
This causes the new issue:
Short story:
1. You create new ad group. You pass owner list to `azuread_group` module, without your user object_id (otherwise it will fail).
2. You decided to update this group by adding/removing some members/owners
3. You forgotten to add yourself to owner list.
4. That leads us to situation where you have `Authorization_RequestDenied` exception (cuz youre not in the owner list)

The problem is with inconsistency of input data. You have to change them during update. 
If you will be able to include yourself in the owner list during group creation, you won't have to change the input data.


Another Thing is that if you add yourself to the list of the owners during group creation. Terraform will throw an exception, but the group will be created anyway -> no state will be generated.

### Description

The permissions `Application.ReadWrite.All` and `Directory.ReadWrite.All` are extremely high privilege permissions on the Azure tenant level and should not be used unless absolutely unavoidable.

The current documentation states:
> When authenticated with a service principal, this resource requires one of the following application roles: Application.ReadWrite.All or Directory.ReadWrite.All
>
> It may be possible to create applications using this resource with the Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy application role, provided the principal being used to run Terraform is included in the owners property. ...

The statement that the permission `Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy` **may** be sufficient is vague and leads engineers to needlessly resort to tenant level write permissions at the first error they face.

There is one common pattern at the moment for which users get 403 with just the `Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy` permission: if you specify additional owners of an azuread_application you, in addition to `Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy` also need `User.Read.All`. This should be added to the documentation.

### Description

<!--- Please leave a helpful description of the feature request here. --->

The `azuread_user` resource supports many properties like `department`, `company` etc, and most notably `account_enabled` -- pretty much all fields I can set manually in AAD.

The `azuread_invitation` doesn't have any of these at all. And again most notably it doesn't have `account_enabled`. At the same time, we can edit and populate all these fields manually in AAD.

We use many external users in our AAD and we use the metadata extensively to document their roles and why they are in our AAD at all.

The proposal is to "beef up" `azuread_invitation` to support all the same properties as `azuread_user` (except there is no need for password of course).

Looking at the graph SDK, the `Invitation` struct does have the `*User` member, and it is the same type being used by `azuread_user`, so in theory this should be just a matter of exposing the properties and fill out this object in `azuread_invitation`?

```go
type Invitation struct {
	ID                      *string          `json:"id,omitempty"`
	InvitedUserDisplayName  *string          `json:"invitedUserDisplayName,omitempty"`
	InvitedUserEmailAddress *string          `json:"invitedUserEmailAddress,omitempty"`
	SendInvitationMessage   *bool            `json:"sendInvitationMessage,omitempty"`
	InviteRedirectURL       *string          `json:"inviteRedirectUrl,omitempty"`
	InviteRedeemURL         *string          `json:"inviteRedeemUrl,omitempty"`
	Status                  *string          `json:"status,omitempty"`
	InvitedUserType         *InvitedUserType `json:"invitedUserType,omitempty"`

	InvitedUserMessageInfo *InvitedUserMessageInfo `json:"invitedUserMessageInfo,omitempty"`
	InvitedUser            *User                   `json:"invitedUser,omitempty"`  // <== THIS
}
```

Of course if this is possible and is implemented, then we'd want `azuread_invitation` to return extra attributes too.

Being able to rely on a more deeply rooted (and hence static-ish) field to reference a user by, simplifies the process of creating config "variations" such as test environments.

In order to achieve this, the User and Users Data Sources, have to support looking up users by on-premise SAM account name.

App Registrations provide for three settings on who can log in:

2.53.0

### Affected Resource(s)

### Terraform Configuration Files

```hcl
resource "azuread_group" "example" {
  display_name            = "example"
  administrative_unit_ids = [ var.administrative_unit_id ]
  security_enabled        = true
}
```

### Output

```
│ Error: Creating group in administrative unit with ID "xxxxx", "example"
│ 
│   with azuread_group.example,
│   on main.tf line 2, in resource "azuread_group" "example":
│   2: resource "azuread_group" "example" {
│ 
│ AdministrativeUnitsClient.BaseClient.Post(): unexpected status 403 with
│ OData error: Authorization_RequestDenied: Insufficient privileges to
│ complete the operation.

```

### Expected Behavior

This is not an unexpected behaviour but a permission issue: to create a group within an administrative, the API permission `Group.ReadWrite.All` is not sufficient: `AdministrativeUnit.Read.All` is also required. Likewise `Groups Administrator` role is not sufficient.

In addition, I find the following wording slightly confusing:

> When authenticated with a service principal, this resource requires one of the following application roles: Group.ReadWrite.All or Directory.ReadWrite.All.`
> [...]
> When authenticated with a user principal, this resource requires one of the following directory roles: Groups Administrator, User Administrator or Global Administrator

Combined with the lack of documentation for the `AdministrativeUnit.Read.All` requirement, this wording gave me the false impressions that directory roles could only be used with user principals and only API permissions could be used with service principals.

### Actual Behavior

I think a slight rewording of the documentation would be helpful. Maybe extending the paragraph dedicated to the case where one want to create a group within an administrative unit, clarifying:

- The need for the user to have read access to the administrative units, for example through the `AdministrativeUnit.Read.All` API permission or `Directory Readers` role (although much this one has much wider permissions than necessary)
- The fact that API permissions cannot be scoped down to an administrative unit, and that if you want to restrict the permissions to this administrative unit, you should use the `Groups Administrator` role scoped on it, even if you're using a service principal

* Please do not leave "+1" or "me too" comments, they generate extra noise for issue followers and do not help prioritise the request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment

### Description

When creating an Azure AD Application in the Azure Portal, the `identifier_uris` field (Application ID URI) defaults to `api://<application_id>`, which is required for using an application to expose APIs. This causes a circular dependency to set it explicitly using the terraform resource, as we don't know the application_id until the application is created.

Proposal is to default the (Application ID URI) `identifier_uris` field to `api://<application_id>` if the attribute isn't set in the resource. If it is set, even to empty `identifier_uris = []` it will not default to `api://....`.

Improve documentation for "azuread_application"

              After speaking with several parties seemingly affected by this issue, for each case it was resolved by double checking the Terraform configuration in question and ensuring that the `owners` field is specified for both the linked application and the service principal itself. We'll seek to document this to help future practitioners from falling afoul here.

To clarify, owners must be set for both the application and the service principal, e.g.

```terraform
data "azuread_client_config" "current" {}

resource "azuread_application" "myapp" {
  display_name = "myapp"
  owners = [
    data.azuread_client_config.current.object_id,
    # ... plus any other desired owners
  ]
}

resource "azuread_service_principal" "myapp" {
  application_id = azuread_application.myapp.application_id
  owners = [
    data.azuread_client_config.current.object_id,
    # ... plus any other desired owners
  ]
}
```

As such I'm going to close this issue as resolved. Terraform appears to be doing the right thing given the correct configuration. If anyone is still experiencing this after double checking their configuration, please feel free to post a further comment _with your exact configuration_ **and** [debug logs](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azuread/latest/docs#logging-and-tracing), and I will be happy to help investigate.

Thanks!

azuread_group: reading a Microsoft 365 group with app-only auth always fails with 403 on Exchange-backed properties

### Community Note

* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 reaction to help the community and maintainers prioritise this request
* Please do not leave "+1" or "me too" comments

### Versions

Provider v3.5.0, and the code path is unchanged on `main` (`groupGetAdditional` in `internal/services/groups/groups.go`).

### Affected Resource

* `azuread_group`

### Description

The group read calls `groupGetAdditional` to fetch `allowExternalSenders`, `autoSubscribeNewMembers`, `hideFromAddressLists` and `hideFromOutlookClients`. Microsoft only exposes these four properties to delegated permissions, so with client-credentials (app-only) auth Graph returns 403 `ErrorAccessDenied` for every Microsoft 365 group, regardless of which application permissions are granted. There's no permission a user can add to fix it.

The result is that `terraform import` or a refresh of any M365 group fails outright under app-only auth:

```
Could not retrieve group with object UID "/groups/<id>": retrieving additional fields:
unexpected status 403 (403 Forbidden) with error: ErrorAccessDenied: Access is denied.
Check credentials and try again.
```

A second effect of the same call: the Exchange backend behind these properties occasionally returns 500, which the SDK retries with backoff. We've measured a single group read blocking for over 4 minutes before surfacing the error.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure the provider with `client_id`/`client_secret` (app-only) auth, e.g. `Directory.Read.All` + `Group.Read.All` granted
2. `terraform import azuread_group.example /groups/<object-id>` of any Microsoft 365 (unified) group

### Proposal

`groupGetAdditional` already tolerates 404 for non-M365 tenants (returns `nil, nil` and proceeds with the properties unset, per microsoftgraph/msgraph-metadata#333). Treating 403 the same way, or skipping the call entirely when auth is app-only, would unblock import/read without a breaking change.

### References

* Relates to #1110. That discussion leans towards splitting these properties into a separate resource, which is a bigger design change; this proposal is a minimal read-side mitigation that works until then.

My use case for this is a clean separation of concerns between user authentication (handled in a separate tenant) and authorization (RBAC on groups).  There are Microsoft Graph APIs available for:
- [Get User in Tenant](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/user-get?view=graph-rest-1.0)

### Debug Output

```
$ terraform apply

Error: checking for duplicate app roles / OAuth2.0 permission scopes: validation failed: duplicate ID found: "c21c916a-31e1-3a42-d62a-21fc26652602"
```

### Expected Behavior

Terraform should be able to create/update an app registration to contain both and app_role (ar) and a  oauth2_permission_scope (ops) given that:
- ops.admin_consent_description == ar.description
- ops.admin_consent_display_name == ar.display_name
- ops.enabled == ar.enabled
- ops.origin == ar.enabled (abstracted away, but defaults to "Application"(?))
- ops.value == ar.value

### Important Factoids

Below you'll find a redacted version of my application manifest. I manually altered and added the app_role with displayName == "Read access", enabling both delegated and application auth flows to access my API with the correct permission (scp & roles).

The root cause of the problem seem to come from [applicationValidateRolesScopes](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azuread/blob/34fc902533a568be58fe18398552ac9e2f13a049/internal/services/applications/applications.go#L312):

```
In Azure Active Directory, application roles (app_role) and permission scopes (oauth2_permission_scope) exported by an application share the same namespace and cannot contain duplicate values
```

### Debug Output

If you don't mind I've encrypted the debug logs (which contain stuff like our subscription ID etc and a lot of stuff I don't understand and don't want to try to sanitise) to the Hashicorp keybase user.

[tflog.log.gz.encrypted.saltpack.zip](https://github.com/terraform-providers/terraform-provider-azuread/files/5101020/tflog.log.gz.encrypted.saltpack.zip)

The error at the end is:
```
Error: patching Azure AD Application with ID "c261c681-ec7d-4854-b577-5c1e4a0570a9": graphrbac.ApplicationsClient#Patch: Failure responding to request: StatusCode=400 -- Original Error: autorest/azure: Service returned an error. Status=400 Code="Unknown" Message="Unknown service error" Details=[{"odata.error":{"code":"Request_BadRequest","date":"2020-08-20T06:05:48","message":{"lang":"en","value":"Property  value cannot be deleted or updated unless it is disabled first."},"requestId":"913e3d7e-ef08-43df-989d-9b0208147973","values":[{"item":"PropertyName","value":"None"},{"item":"PropertyErrorCode","value":"CannotDeleteEnabledEntitlement"}]}}]
```

### Panic Output
None

### Expected Behavior

The appRoles should be created once, and I should never experience the above error.

### Actual Behavior

During resource creation, the appRoles are created (PATCH-ed onto the app), then they are disabled (PATCH-ed into `isEnabled: false`). Then they are deleted and replaced with new copies (new appRoles with new IDs are PATCH-ed onto the app). 

Then, sometimes (not always) I experience a `Property  value cannot be deleted or updated unless it is disabled first.` error. This looks like a dodgy error and behaviour from Azure AD, however I think it may be being exacerbated by the fact that we delete and recreate app roles close together while creating an app (they fact that this occurs only sometimes makes this feel like a race condition and Azure AD is full of frustrating eventual consistency).

I've had a poke through the provider code, and I believe we:
* First patch the new appRoles onto the app here inside `resourceApplicationCreate`: https://github.com/terraform-providers/terraform-provider-azuread/blob/3892ca120ee9dcc6d63fabcc124306cebea019e7/azuread/resource_application.go#L389-L399
* Then we perform a `resourceApplicationUpdate` at the end of `resourceApplicationCreate`. Inside this function, we patch the the appRoles disabled here: https://github.com/terraform-providers/terraform-provider-azuread/blob/3892ca120ee9dcc6d63fabcc124306cebea019e7/azuread/resource_application.go#L516-L519 (this appears to be because the ResourceData still thinks there are no appRoles, even though we previously created them, so HasChanges must be returning true)
* We then create new roles with new IDs here: https://github.com/terraform-providers/terraform-provider-azuread/blob/3892ca120ee9dcc6d63fabcc124306cebea019e7/azuread/resource_application.go#L522 and patch it onto the app here: https://github.com/terraform-providers/terraform-provider-azuread/blob/3892ca120ee9dcc6d63fabcc124306cebea019e7/azuread/resource_application.go#L542 (thereby trying to delete the old roles and replace them with the new ones).

Seems to me like we could just delete the code that is creating the app roles inside `resourceApplicationCreate` and leave it to `resourceApplicationUpdate` to create them? 

I'm not certain that this is the thing that's causing the above error, but I believe only the oauth2Permissions and the appRoles have this sort "disable before deleting" error, and it seems reasonable that we should only create appRoles once during application creation.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `terraform apply`

If the bug does not happen, you may need to repeat the following steps as quickly as you can:
2. `terraform destroy`
3. `terraform apply`

Eventually, it happens.

# Support for Publisher Domain Configuration in azuread_application Resource

## Community Note

* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 reaction to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* Please do not leave "+1" or "me too" comments, they generate extra noise for issue followers and do not help prioritize the request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment

## Description

Add support for configuring the **publisher domain** as an input parameter in the `azuread_application` resource. Currently, `publisher_domain` is only available as a read-only computed attribute, requiring manual configuration through the Azure Portal or Microsoft Graph API calls.

## Use Case

**Publisher domain verification** is crucial for:
- **Removing "unverified" app warnings** in Azure AD consent screens
- **Improving user trust** during authentication flows
- **Meeting enterprise security requirements** for multi-tenant applications
- **Ensuring consistent branding** across Azure AD applications

Currently, users must manually:
1. Create domain verification files (`microsoft-identity-association.json`)
2. Host files at `/.well-known/microsoft-identity-association.json`
3. Use Azure Portal or custom API scripts to verify domains
4. Manage domain verification outside of Terraform workflows

## Proposed Enhancement

Add `publisher_domain` as an optional input parameter to `azuread_application`:

```hcl
resource "azuread_application" "example" {
  display_name      = "My Application"
  sign_in_audience  = "AzureADMultipleOrgs"
  
  # NEW: Publisher domain configuration
  publisher_domain = "example.com"
  
  # Existing configuration...
  web {
    redirect_uris = ["https://example.com/auth/callback"]
  }
}
```

## Current Limitation

```hcl
# ❌ This doesn't work - publisher_domain is read-only
resource "azuread_application" "example" {
  display_name     = "My App"
  publisher_domain = "example.com"  # Error: Unsupported argument
}

# ✅ Only available as output
output "current_publisher_domain" {
  value = azuread_application.example.publisher_domain
}
```

## API Support

The Microsoft Graph API **already supports** publisher domain configuration:

```bash
# PATCH /applications/{id}
curl -X PATCH "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/applications/{id}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"publisherDomain": "example.com"}'
```

## Current Workarounds

**1. Manual Azure Portal Configuration**
- Time-consuming and not infrastructure-as-code
- Requires manual intervention in CI/CD pipelines

**2. Custom API Scripts** (what we currently use):
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Custom script to set publisher domain
APPLICATION_ID="$1"
DOMAIN="$2"

az rest --method PATCH \
  --url "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/applications/$APPLICATION_ID" \
  --body "{\"publisherDomain\": \"$DOMAIN\"}"
```

**3. Terraform + local-exec Provisioner**:
```hcl
resource "null_resource" "publisher_domain" {
  depends_on = [azuread_application.example]
  
  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command = "./scripts/set-publisher-domain.sh ${azuread_application.example.client_id} ${var.publisher_domain}"
  }
}
```

## Benefits of Native Terraform Support

**✅ Infrastructure as Code**
- Declarative publisher domain management
- Version-controlled domain configuration
- Reproducible deployments across environments

**✅ Simplified Workflows**
- No additional scripts or manual steps required
- Integrated with existing Terraform Azure AD workflows
- Automatic domain verification handling

**✅ Better DX (Developer Experience)**
- Consistent with other `azuread_application` attributes
- Type safety and validation through Terraform
- Plan/apply visibility for domain changes

## Implementation Considerations

**Domain Verification Requirements:**
- Domain must be verified before assignment
- Should validate domain ownership via `/.well-known/microsoft-identity-association.json`
- Could provide helpful error messages for unverified domains

**Backward Compatibility:**
- Optional parameter (default: `null`)
- Existing `publisher_domain` output remains unchanged
- No breaking changes to current configurations

**Validation:**
- Ensure domain format is valid
- Check domain verification status
- Provide clear error messages for verification failures

## Example Implementation

```hcl
resource "azuread_application" "datadog_vending_machine" {
```

### Description

This is a feature request to extend the `reply_url` on `azuread_application` to allow a brand new type of reply urls implemented in Azure AD called "Spa".

They differ from the traditional "Web" reply urls in that they support OAuth2's PKCE, see [here](https://github.com/AzureAD/microsoft-authentication-library-for-js/tree/dev/lib/msal-browser#prerequisites) on how to change it in the manifest, and [here](https://github.com/AzureAD/microsoft-authentication-library-for-js/issues/1000) for the discussion on a client. Essentially, reply urls will have two types, "Web" (current) and "Spa" (new addition).

Currently, terraform only supports an array of strings, which represent reply urls of type "Web". We need to extend it to support either an array of strings (for backward compatibility) or an array of maps containing two keys, e.g. "reply_url" and "type", where "type" can only be "Web" or "Spa".

FYI I have validated that changing the type does indeed make PKCE work.

### Description

The `azuread_group` resource's `behaviors` argument validates against a hardcoded list of allowed `resourceBehaviorOptions` values in `internal/services/groups/constants.go`. The Microsoft Graph API supports a `ProvisionSiteOnDemand` value for `resourceBehaviorOptions` on M365 (Unified) groups, but this value is not included in the provider's validation list, so Terraform rejects it.

From https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/group-set-options:

> **ProvisionSiteOnDemand**: By default, a SharePoint site is automatically provisioned when a Microsoft 365 group is created. Use this option to override the default behavior so that the site is provisioned on demand.

This is useful for M365 groups created solely for mail-enabled notification purposes (e.g., Defender for Cloud alert routing) where a SharePoint site, OneNote notebook, and associated resources are unnecessary. Without `ProvisionSiteOnDemand`, every M365 group created via Terraform automatically provisions a SharePoint team site that is never used, creating resource sprawl, compliance scope, and storage overhead.

**Current behavior** — setting `"ProvisionSiteOnDemand"` in `behaviors` produces:

```text
Error: expected behaviors.0 to be one of [AllowOnlyMembersToPost CalendarMemberReadOnly
ConnectorsDisabled HideGroupInOutlook SkipExchangeInstantOn
SubscribeMembersToCalendarEventsDisabled SubscribeNewGroupMembers WelcomeEmailDisabled],
got ProvisionSiteOnDemand
```

**Expected behavior** — `"ProvisionSiteOnDemand"` should be accepted as a valid `behaviors` value and passed through to the Microsoft Graph API as a `resourceBehaviorOptions` entry during group creation (`POST /groups`).

**Suggested fix** — add the constant and include it in the validation slice in `internal/services/groups/constants.go`:

```go
const (
    // ... existing constants ...
    GroupResourceBehaviorOptionProvisionSiteOnDemand = "ProvisionSiteOnDemand"
)

var possibleValuesForGroupResourceBehaviorOptions = []string{
    // ... existing values ...
    GroupResourceBehaviorOptionProvisionSiteOnDemand,
}
```

I have a PR ready to submit that implements this change (plus matching updates to `docs/resources/group.md` and `docs/resources/group_without_members.md`).

### New or Affected Resource(s)

- `azuread_group`
- `azuread_group_without_members`

### Potential Terraform Configuration

```hcl
resource "azuread_group" "notify" {
  display_name     = "defender-alerts-notify"
  mail_enabled     = true
  mail_nickname    = "defender-alerts-notify"
  security_enabled = false
  types            = ["Unified"]

  behaviors = [
    "HideGroupInOutlook",
    "WelcomeEmailDisabled",
    "ProvisionSiteOnDemand",
  ]
}
```

### References

- Microsoft Graph — [Microsoft 365 group behaviors and provisioning options](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/group-set-options) — documents `ProvisionSiteOnDemand` as a supported `resourceBehaviorOptions` value
- Microsoft Graph — [group resource type — resourceBehaviorOptions property](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/group) — confirms `resourceBehaviorOptions` can only be set at group creation time

* When the **owners** parameter is removed, terraform **detects a change** and also shows that modifications were completed successfully.

* However, it **fails to actually remove** the owners from the azuread_application resource (therefore, the next apply shows an ***update-in-place*** where it tries to remove the owners **again**)

```hcl
        tags                           = []
        # (14 unchanged attributes hidden)

Apply complete! Resources: 0 added, 1 changed, 0 destroyed.
```

```hcl
Terraform will perform the following actions:
```

3. `terraform apply` (after removing the owners parameter)
4. `terraform apply`

### Important Factoids
* A similar issue was raised previously where terraform didn't detect a change in the owners parameter and hence, couldn't remove the owners.  [https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azuread/issues/353](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azuread/issues/353)

* A fix was merged for the same which allows specifying owners an an empty list and enables the removal of owners.

* However, currently, the changes are detected but terraform isn't able to remove the owners
